description.value: A pilot fMRI study examined brain responses to visual food cues and milkshake taste in healthy-weight and overweight children aged 6–8 years, including interactions with parent-reported eating behavior.

spans.text: This pilot study provides preliminary evidence of feasibility of studying young children’s taste processing and suggests a possible developmental shift in brain response to taste.

value: We predicted that brain response to food cues (anticipatory reward) and tastes (consummatory reward) would be heightened in children with BMI > 85  %ile compared to those in a healthy weight.
